title: Revise study capability M1 design to answer review 1
summary: Revise docs/design/study-capability-m1.md so it answers every finding in study-capability-m1-review-1.md (7 major, 8 minor, 2 nits). The review's eight 'decisions for the user' are settled from BRIEF.md where it speaks and decided by the author where it doesn't. Design only: no code, and the review file is untouched.

defaults_applied.how: The revision keeps alternatives and reversal costs for every changed decision. The design is returned for independent re-review before any build.
Each answered finding and each settled decision cites BRIEF.md lines or review sections. Cost and reversal figures stay labeled as estimates.
The brief and the review's decision list supply the user's answers, so no question is asked.
One file is revised. No code is written and no governance file changes.
The response is written so an outside reader can follow it without the review's context.
Rules stay mechanical with planted-fault tests, or are explicitly relabeled as verifier duties (prose-only).
Run-output redaction and credential handling are designed in, and nothing secret is written.

assumptions: 'Review 1' means docs/design/reviews/study-capability-m1-review-1.md, and 'the study design' means docs/design/study-capability-m1.md. This is the only design with a review that is still unanswered.

'The brief settles its questions' means the review's eight 'Decisions for the user' are resolved from BRIEF.md wherever it speaks, and the rest are my call. Likely outcomes, to be confirmed by the producer: containment is built into the capability (BRIEF.md:313 and v0 §16.2), all BRIEF.md:298 streams are required, Pages publishing becomes a named required design for M1 (BRIEF.md:395), and the evidence rules cannot be waived.
The response lives inside the design doc (a response section plus revised sections). The review file is a historical record and is not edited.
This is a revision of the design only. The design's gate requires that majors are answered before any build, so no build is started.
A re-review is not part of this job. The design's status line says it is awaiting re-review.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/study-capability-m1.md answers every finding in study-capability-m1-review-1.md (M1–M7, m1–m8, n1–n2) by id, in a response table or section, each marked accepted (with the change made), or declined (with a reason). None is left unanswered.

Each of the eight 'Decisions for the user' is settled in the design with a stated basis. Where BRIEF.md settles it, the line is cited: BRIEF.md:298 for all observability streams (M7); 110-111 for the recorded cap, kill switch and downgrade blocker (m6); 299 for redaction (M6); 313 for trust and prompt injection (M5, m7); 306 for the M4 model scope; 395 for Pages being part of M1 (m1). Any decision the brief does not settle is made by the author, with the reason recorded.

§5.4 is revised: the six evidence rules are non-waivable (M1); citation rules cover commit, pull-request and run ids, `study.run/1` carries the SHA, and `both` requires a file source and a run source (M2); the four judgment rules are rewritten as structural checks (`contradicts` link, `quote` field, typed Quantity, template-only provenance) or relabeled as verifier duties (M3). Every rule that remains labeled mechanical can be tested with one planted fault and one clean case.

§5.1 and §5.3 are extended or bounded for M4: parallel agents, fan-out/join, an evaluated-by field on guards, unhandled failures, what a retry changes, and a timeout for an unanswered person. The synthetic example is corrected so the bound, the counter and the 'requeued' wording agree (m2).

The run step (§2, `study.run/1`) names containment and credential handling, a redaction step before output is stored, which meter enforces the per-run cap and what happens when it cannot be observed, the capture streams, and a replay step (M5, M6, M7, m6). The design also covers fresh-context isolation and the capability-gap log (m8), and the prompt-injection limit (m7).

Remaining minors and nits are handled: a rationale-card completeness rule (m3), observed-transition recording and scenario independence (m4), A2-C, A4-B and A1-C reworded fairly with a 'typed records now, export later' option (m5), A3 choice moved into the table (n1), and the BRIEF commit named (n2). The §7 reversal costs are updated for any new decision.

The status header no longer says the findings are unanswered, and the design remains design-only. No crate, Rust code, or governance file is changed. The review file is untouched. The design makes no claim about firstmate, and its examples stay labeled synthetic.

Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` from the repo root. They pass, including the xtask policy tests, which may check doc links and anchors. Run `git diff --stat` and confirm only docs/ files changed.

out_of_scope: Creating the athena-cap-study crate or any Rust code, tests, or Cargo.toml changes
Writing the Pages publishing design (named as a required follow-up only)
Reading, running or modeling firstmate, or making any claim about it
Editing BRIEF.md or the review file
Writing a second review of the revised design
Changing governance files such as athena.toml or defaults.toml
departures: Cost and time are slightly above the reference. The doc is long, 17 findings must each be answered, and the verifier must cross-check every finding id against the revised sections. Acceptance is somewhat lower because 'decide the rest yourself' leaves room for the user to disagree.
